title: NACHOVA AND OTHERS v. BULGARIA
summary: In Nachova and Others v. Bulgaria, the applicants—Ms. Anelia Kunchova Nachova, her mother Ms. Aksiniya Hristova, and the parents of Private Petkov—are Bulgarian nationals who identify as being of Romany origin, thus falling within the Council of Europe’s definition of Roma and Travellers. The case centres on the vulnerability of Roma individuals to excessive use of force and potential racial discrimination by state authorities. On 19 July 1996, Privates Angelov and Petkov, both young Roma conscripts, were killed by military police during an attempted arrest after escaping from a military-detention facility in Lesura, Bulgaria. Neither man was armed, and the operation involved heavily armed officers who fired multiple shots, resulting in the deaths of both privates as they tried to flee. The applicants alleged that the use of lethal force was unjustified and that the authorities failed to investigate possible racist motives behind the killings. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Articles 2 (right to life), 13 (right to an effective remedy), and 14 (prohibition of discrimination), finding the applications admissible and warranting a full examination of the facts and legal issues. This case is significant as it highlights the persistent risks Roma and Traveller communities face regarding police violence and the need for thorough investigations into possible discriminatory motives, reflecting broader historical patterns of marginalisation in Europe.
